user.title: Connect to your HDMI matrix
user.description: Enter the address of the matrix web interface. Leave the credentials empty if the matrix has no login configured.

data_description.use_default_credentials: Ticked, this ignores the two fields below and signs in with the factory defaults. Untick it if you changed the login on the matrix.
data_description.host: IP address or hostname, for example 192.168.1.60
data_description.username: The user you sign in with on the matrix web interface, not your Home Assistant account

discovery_confirm.title: Set up {name}
discovery_confirm.description: A {name} was found at {host}. Enter its web interface credentials, or leave them empty if it has no login configured.

data_description.use_default_credentials: Ticked, this ignores the two fields below and signs in with the factory defaults. Untick it if you changed the login on the matrix.
data_description.username: The user you sign in with on the matrix web interface, not your Home Assistant account

reauth_confirm.title: Re-enter your matrix credentials
reauth_confirm.description: The matrix at {host} no longer accepts the stored credentials.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect. Check the address and that the matrix is powered on.
error.unsupported_device: That address answered, but not like an HDCVT matrix.

abort.already_configured: This matrix is already set up.
abort.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the discovered matrix.
abort.unsupported_device: The discovered device is not a supported HDCVT matrix.

data_description.scan_interval: How often to re-read the matrix. Its web backend handles one request at a time, so shorter is not always better.
